---
title: Text
description: "Free-form strings encoded by a frozen text model."
---

A payment description can carry detail beyond the merchant label, such as
whether the charge is a delivery order. `Text` encodes those free-form strings
with a frozen Hugging Face model. relflow learns to combine their representations
with the amount and other fields. It does not fine-tune that encoder or
generate text.

Install the optional text dependency:

```bash
uv add "relflow[text]"
```

```python
import relflow as rf

model = rf.Model.xs(
    amount=rf.Number,
    merchant=rf.Category,
    memo=rf.Text,
    disputed=rf.Boolean(mask=True),
)
```

One labeled payment:

```yaml
amount: 84.50
merchant: North Market
memo: "North Market delivery order"
disputed: false
```

## Input and options

The Arrow leaf must contain strings. An empty string is valued; a null has a
separate state. Tokenization pads and truncates at `max_length`.

| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `model` | `"google/bert_uncased_L-2_H-128_A-2"` | Hugging Face identifier or local model path. |
| `max_length` | `128` | Positive tokenization length limit. |
| `tokenizer_batch_size` | `4096` | Maximum strings materialized per tokenizer call. |
| `encoder_batch_size` | `32` | Maximum flattened text values per frozen-encoder call. |
| `encoder_pooling` | `"cls"` | `"cls"`, `"mean"`, or `"pooler"`; the last requires `pooler_output`. |
| `cache` | `True` | Automatic tiered reuse; a positive integer also caps hot entries. `False` disables caching. |
| `store` | `None` | Writable local cache directory; defaults to the platform cache directory. |
| `resident` | `None` | Device table and replacement workspace budget in MiB. CUDA defaults to one eighth of free memory, capped at 512 MiB; other devices default to `0`. |
| `memory` | `None` | Shared Rust RAM cache budget in MiB; defaults to 64. `0` answers through disk. |
| `objective` | `"l2"` | Embedding reconstruction loss: `"l1"` or `"l2"`. |
| `jitter` | `rf.Jitter()` | Training noise on the pooled frozen embedding before learned projection. |

`cls` and `mean` require `last_hidden_state`. Text fields using the same model
reuse its frozen encoder within the process. Right-padded values are grouped
by length and cropped per encoder batch; left-padded values retain their full
width. `max_length` controls truncation and the persisted token-row width;
cached loader batches carry IDs regardless of that limit.

## Automatic reuse

The default `rf.Text` configuration reuses tokenizer results and pristine frozen
embeddings across fields, splits, and runs. Loader workers send one integer ID
per text slot. The trainer resolves these IDs through three tiers:

1. A bounded device table retains frequently reused vectors. Resident hits
   avoid transferring vectors from the host.
2. A shared Rust Moka cache admits frequently observed entries to RAM. All
   loader workers belonging to the trainer share this cache owner.
3. A SQLite store retains token rows and frozen vectors on local disk.
   Eviction from either hot tier leaves the disk entry available.

A true miss runs the frozen encoder in the trainer on its configured device.
The cache acknowledges a new vector after its disk transaction commits. Other
clients of that owner wait for an in-progress fill and can retry it if the
encoding client disconnects. Texts with identical token rows, including after
truncation, share one canonical ID within their tokenizer configuration.
Nulls and empty strings retain their distinct states.

Memory use follows the hot budgets rather than the total number of distinct
texts. SQLite keeps its private page cache at 4 MiB and does not map the
entire database. Rust admission uses approximate frequency, so a scan of new
text need not evict the descriptions repeatedly used by training. Device
admission also considers frequency and recency. These policies choose useful
entries; they do not guarantee an exact global ranking.

The default needs no cache configuration. To choose a local disk and tighter
hot budgets:

```python
memo = rf.Text(store="embeddings/payment-memos", memory=32, resident=128)
```

`memory` bounds charged hot payload and entry overhead, rather than total
process RSS. Python/Rust runtime overhead, active batches, the SQLite page
cache, and the operating system's file cache are additional. Device tables
share a budget across live encoder variants on that device, reserving space
for replacement tables and index workspace. `cache=N` additionally limits
hot entries; cold disk entries remain available. `cache=False` skips all
cache tiers and tokenizes and encodes each batch directly.

The disk store grows with observed aliases, token rows, and vector variants;
there is no automatic disk quota or pruning. Place it on storage sized for
the workload. `RELFLOW_CACHE_DIR` changes the default directory for the
application; otherwise relflow uses `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, `LOCALAPPDATA`, or
`~/.cache`, under `relflow/artifacts-v1`. Use a local filesystem that supports
SQLite locking. Existing NPY stores are left intact; this format creates a
new `artifacts.sqlite3` and fills it as text is observed.

Text uses the shared tensorfield artifact cache. Its standard owner isolates
Rust Moka and SQLite from encoder libraries. The optional `relflow-native` add-on
uses the same storage format and accelerates transport and lookups without
changing the Text schema. Other extensions can reuse the shared store with
their own payload codecs and identities.

One owner serves a trainer's loader family through authenticated loopback
connections, including spawned workers. Independently started trainers and
DDP ranks have separate RAM budgets and connections to the same disk store;
RAM is not shared across machines. The owner exits when its parent releases
it or exits. If it fails during a run, recreate the model and loaders to
reopen the durable store. A writable cache directory and local loopback
connections are required.

Encoder weight contents and configuration, tokenizer vocabulary and settings,
pooling, device type, and encoder precision distinguish entries. Trainable
projections and training jitter run after lookup on every forward pass,
preserving gradients and fresh noise. Checkpoints retain the request settings
and learned weights, and omit cache contents, connections, and device tables.
A loaded model can reuse compatible disk entries.

This is a general reuse mechanism for frozen text encoders. Its throughput
benefit depends on repeated text, the working set, storage speed, and worker
cost. A mostly unique stream still performs tokenization, encoding, and disk
writes. Measure the complete data loop when choosing worker counts and
budgets; extra workers can cost more than they save once text is cached.

## Warming the cache

To fill the cache ahead of training, provide the application-supplied
`memo_texts` as a string sequence or Arrow column:

```python
model.nodes[rf.Address("memo")].embedder.warm(memo_texts)
```

Run the warmer on the device and under the autocast context training will
use, since precision is part of the key. Nulls are skipped and repeated
strings count once. The return value counts newly persisted vectors.
No explicit `store` setting is required.

## Learning and output

A reconstructing mask trains the decoder against the pristine frozen embedding,
using state loss and the configured content objective on valued targets.
[Jitter](../reference/jitter.qmd) affects only visible continuous inputs,
not strings, token IDs, or target embeddings. Both settings of
`jitter.normalize` act at the same pooled-embedding boundary.

Text has no decoded public state/content payload. `embed=True` exports a
contextual relflow embedding, distinct from the frozen encoder output; see
[shared leaf options](index.qmd#shared-leaf-options).
Use [Vector](vector.qmd) when the source already supplies an embedding.

## External model assets

The first use of a remote model identifier may download tokenizer and encoder
assets. relflow checkpoints save the request and learned relflow weights,
but do not bundle those external assets. Every loading or serving process
must be able to resolve the same identifier or local path. For reproducible
deployment, prepare a pinned encoder directory and ship it with the artifact.
